title: Pullback compatibility of the derived-to-ordinary tensor comparison
statement:
Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),R)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),S)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi with commutative ring sheaves on sites small in a common coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Use module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $[A]$ for localization of a complex, $T(A,B)=\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes B)$ for the signed direct-sum total [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and $\rho_{A,B}:[A]\otimes^{\mathbf L}[B]\to[T(A,B)]$ for the canonical map obtained by tensoring K-flat resolution augmentations [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent, lem-sfb-ringed-derived-tensor-augmentation-naturality]. Let $\alpha_A:Lf^*[A]\to[f^*A]$ be the canonical left-derived comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], and let $\mu_{[A],[B]}:Lf^*([A]\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}[B])\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf^*[A]\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Lf^*[B]$ be the canonical pullback tensor isomorphism $\mu$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] (the one used by the relative cup product), i.e. the canonical derived tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] computed on K-flat resolutions with flat terms by the representative normalization of [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-tensor-canonical-shift-unit]. Write $\delta_{A,B}:f^*T(A,B)\xrightarrow{\sim}T(f^*A,f^*B)$ for the totalization of the ordinary tensor comparison normalized by $r\otimes(a\otimes b)\mapsto(r\otimes a)\otimes(1\otimes b)$ after the inverse-image tensor identification [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison, lem-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison-construction]. For arbitrary unbounded complexes $A,B$ of $S$-modules, the following equality holds in $D(R)$:
$$[\delta_{A,B}]\circ\alpha_{T(A,B)}\circ Lf^*(\rho_{A,B})=\rho_{f^*A,f^*B}\circ(\alpha_A\otimes^{\mathbf L}\alpha_B)\circ\mu_{[A],[B]}.$$
There is no flatness hypothesis on the structural ring map or on $A,B$.

proof.text: Choose quasi-isomorphisms $p:P\to A$, $q:Q\to B$ with $P,Q$ K-flat and termwise flat. The resolution theorem applies on the two given small ringed sites, without a bound on the complexes. Put $C=T(P,Q)$ and $c=T(p,q):C\to T(A,B)$. The total-tensor model theorem makes $C$ K-flat with flat terms. Pullback preserves these properties for $P,Q$. Consequently the derived pullback comparisons $\alpha_P,\alpha_Q,\alpha_C$ are invertible. Neither $c$ nor its ordinary pullback is asserted to be a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0FPH, label lemma-tensor-pull-compatibility, proof: the resolution diagram.

proof.text:
Write $s=[p]\otimes^{\mathbf L}[q]$ and $e=\rho_{P,Q}\circ s^{-1}:[A]\otimes^{\mathbf L}[B]\xrightarrow{\sim}[C]$. The tensor augmentation theorem gives $\rho_{A,B}=[c]\circ e$. Set $\theta=\alpha_C\circ Lf^*(e)$; this is an isomorphism onto $[f^*C]$. Naturality of the left-derived comparison, applied to the actual cochain map $c$, gives
$$\alpha_{T(A,B)}Lf^*(\rho_{A,B})=[f^*c]\theta.$$
This uses naturality before any cancellation; it does not require invertibility of $\alpha_{T(A,B)}$.

source.place: Tag 0FPH, label lemma-tensor-pull-compatibility, proof: the resolution diagram.

proof.text:
By the representative normalization of the canonical pullback tensor isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-tensor-canonical-shift-unit], at the K-flat flat-term pair $P,Q$ with $C=T(P,Q)$ one has $\mu_{[P],[Q]}=(\alpha_P^{-1}\otimes^{\mathbf L}\alpha_Q^{-1})\,r_{f^*P,f^*Q}\,[c_{P,Q}]\,\alpha_C\,Lf^*(r_{P,Q}^{-1})$, where $r$ denotes the representative isomorphisms of the K-flat derived tensor and $c_{P,Q}$ the cochain comparison of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]; $f^*P,f^*Q$ are again K-flat with flat terms by Step 1, so $r_{f^*P,f^*Q}$ is defined. The tensor augmentation theorem gives $\rho_{P,Q}=r_{P,Q}^{-1}$ and $\rho_{f^*P,f^*Q}=r_{f^*P,f^*Q}^{-1}$. The cochain maps $c_{P,Q}$ and $\delta_{P,Q}$ agree: on each bidegree summand both are the ordinary module tensor comparison $r\otimes(x\otimes y)\mapsto(r\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$ on local pure tensors [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison], and maps out of a sheafified tensor product are determined by local pure tensors. Substituting and moving the invertible factors gives
$$\rho_{f^*P,f^*Q}(\alpha_P\otimes^{\mathbf L}\alpha_Q)\mu_{[P],[Q]}=[\delta_{P,Q}]\alpha_C Lf^*(\rho_{P,Q}).$$
The $\mu$ of the projection-mate node is this canonical comparison, the unique natural transformation with these components, as the statement specifies; no independently chosen isomorphism is used.

source.place: Tag 0FPH, label lemma-tensor-pull-compatibility, proof: the resolution diagram.

proof.text:
Apply naturality of $\rho$ to $f^*p,f^*q$ and naturality of $\alpha$ separately to $p,q$. Combining these equalities with Step 3 and cancelling the isomorphism $Lf^*s$ gives
$$\rho_{f^*A,f^*B}(\alpha_A\otimes^{\mathbf L}\alpha_B)\mu_{[A],[B]}=[T(f^*p,f^*q)]\,[\delta_{P,Q}]\theta.$$
Explicitly, before cancellation naturality of $\mu$ replaces $\mu_{[A],[B]}Lf^*s$ by $(Lf^*[p]\otimes^{\mathbf L}Lf^*[q])\mu_{[P],[Q]}$; naturality of $\alpha$ replaces each $\alpha_A Lf^*[p]$ by $[f^*p]\alpha_P$; naturality of $\rho$ then combines the two pulled-back maps into $[T(f^*p,f^*q)]$.

source.place: Tag 0FPH, label lemma-tensor-pull-compatibility, proof: the resolution diagram.

proof.text:
Ordinary tensor naturality gives the cochain equality
$$\delta_{A,B}\,f^*c=T(f^*p,f^*q)\,\delta_{P,Q}.$$
On a summand of bidegree $(i,j)$ both sides send $r\otimes(x\otimes y)$ to $(r\otimes p(x))\otimes(1\otimes q(y))$. The ordinary comparison is natural on module sheaves, and its totalization is the cochain comparison of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence], natural in both complex arguments, so these equalities pass to each direct-sum summand; the signed total differential agrees since the maps preserve bidegrees. Localize this equality and compose with $\theta$. Step 2 identifies its left side with the left side of the required formula, and Step 4 identifies its right side with the right side. This proves the formula for arbitrary $A,B$ and arbitrary structural ring map.
